title: CRISPR-SID: Identifying EZH2 as a druggable target for desmoid tumors via in vivo dependency mapping.
authors: Naert, Thomas; Tulkens, Dieter; Van Nieuwenhuysen, Tom; Przybyl, Joanna; Demuynck, Suzan; van de Rijn, Matt; Al-Jazrawe, Mushriq; Alman, Benjamin A; Coucke, Paul J; De Leeneer, Kim; Vanhove, Christian; Savvides, Savvas N; Creytens, David; Vleminckx, Kris
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
one_liner_zh: 该文利用CRISPR-SID和深度学习预测双链断裂修复模式，在体内鉴定结缔组织增生性肿瘤的遗传依赖靶点（如EZH2），但核心是肿瘤药物靶点发现，而非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制建模，仅涉及转录因子CREB3L1作为依赖基因，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: Cancer precision medicine implies identification of tumor-specific vulnerabilities associated with defined oncogenic pathways. Desmoid tumors are soft-tissue neoplasms strictly driven by Wnt signaling network hyperactivation. Despite this clearly defined genetic etiology and the strict and unique implication of the Wnt/beta-catenin pathway, no specific molecular targets for these tumors have been identified. To address this caveat, we developed fast, efficient, and penetrant genetic Xenopus tropicalis desmoid tumor models to identify and characterize drug targets. We used multiplexed CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing in these models to simultaneously target a tumor suppressor gene (apc) and candidate dependency genes. Our methodology CRISPR/Cas9 selection-mediated identification of dependencies (CRISPR-SID) uses calculated deviations between experimentally observed gene editing outcomes and deep-learning-predicted double-strand break repair patterns to identify genes under negative selection during tumorigenesis. This revealed EZH2 and SUZ12, both encoding polycomb repressive complex 2 components, and the transcription factor CREB3L1 as genetic dependencies for desmoid tumors. In vivo EZH2 inhibition by Tazemetostat induced partial regression of established autochthonous tumors. In vitro models of patient desmoid tumor cells revealed a direct effect of Tazemetostat on Wnt pathway activity. CRISPR-SID represents a potent approach for in vivo mapping of tumor vulnerabilities and drug target identification.
abstract_zh: 癌症精准医学意味着识别与特定致癌通路相关的肿瘤特异性弱点。硬纤维瘤（desmoid tumors）是由Wnt信号网络过度激活严格驱动的软组织肿瘤。尽管具有明确界定的遗传病因学以及Wnt/β-catenin通路的严格且独特参与，但尚未为这些肿瘤识别出特异性分子靶点。为解决这一缺陷，我们开发了快速、高效且具有高外显率的遗传性热带爪蟾（Xenopus tropicalis）硬纤维瘤模型，以识别和表征药物靶点。我们在这些模型中使用多重CRISPR/Cas9基因组编辑，同时靶向一个肿瘤抑制基因（apc）和候选依赖性基因。我们的方法CRISPR/Cas9选择介导的依赖性识别（CRISPR-SID）利用实验观察到的基因编辑结果与深度学习预测的双链断裂修复模式之间的计算偏差，来识别肿瘤发生过程中处于负选择下的基因。这揭示了EZH2和SUZ12（两者均编码多梳抑制复合物2组分）以及转录因子CREB3L1作为硬纤维瘤的遗传依赖性。体内EZH2抑制通过Tazemetostat诱导已建立的自发性肿瘤部分消退。患者硬纤维瘤细胞的体外模型显示Tazemetostat对Wnt通路活性的直接效应。CRISPR-SID代表了一种用于体内肿瘤弱点映射和药物靶点识别的强效方法。
